parts:
Dear everyone!

First of all, this is my first project (Master Thesis) with unmarked/R and my first “bigger project” in total, so please excuse any obscurities in phrasing my R/ statical problem.
I am interested in modelling detection probability and abundance for multiple bird-species using repeated point counts.
I used consecutively repeated point counts (4 five-minute counts, summing up to 20 minutes) during a single season that was devided into 2 periods (first and second half of breeding season, both 6 weeks long).
Breeding code, location and detection were related to each individual for all counts.
In total, I conducted surveys at 81 locations, 8 only visited in the first period, 18 only in the second and 55 in both periods (so that I have two times four five minute counts for latter). For the SiteCovs, I use relative habitat composition for all locations (e.g. urban area 0.8, forest area 0.15, open area 0.05). For the ObsCovs, I use day number (of the year) and start time (in minutes relative to sunrise).

My first (there are probably more to come) question concerns the fitting functions:
1.) Am I right with assuming that pcount is the best fitting function for my case, or am I better off with a different fitting function (mPois maybe?)? 
My habitat-SiteCovs stay the same for all counts (no matter if 4 or 8 counts were made), but my ObsCovs do not (day number varies between periods, start time varies between all counts). 
I have prepared a script for the unmarked frame and it is working. I THINK, I also understood that, as I have sitecovs for all locations and all obscovs missing do not haveaccording observations anyway, no data will be lost in my frame, right?
I THINK (again :) ), that I am better off using pcount than mPois, as I am able to use all counts of both periods (and therefore can also use species with less observations, some of which will probably cause problems if I have to split up into both periods)?

2.) Is it somehow possible to use the "observer" as a covariate aswell to see if I, for example, start missing a specific species after three counts for example (due to concentration for instance)? I was the only observer, but I would like to see, if possible, if there is any influence on my observations as I counted for 20 minutes. Would this just be another data frame in the obsCovs with 8 columns looking something like: obsCovs [[3]] [1] = A,B,C,D,A,B,C,D? 


Anyways, I added the script for the UMF and the data for one of the species (but please try not to pay too much attention to the efficiency of the script, as I said, I'm only at the beginning with R/unmarked/modelling). 
Please let me know if I need to explain something in more detail. Every advice is immensely helpful,

Thank you very much, Christian
